COURSEPILOT · 3-WEEK ROADMAP

From semester planner to AI counselor.

Three focused weeks from today’s scheduling demo to a conversational agent that understands a student, recommends courses with reasons, and turns advice into an approvable plan.

Final product · AI agent counselor · Cornell Engineering CS
WEEK 01 · FOUNDATION

Know the student and the rules

Build the academic ground truth the agent will trust.

Model a narrow, sourced slice of Cornell Engineering CS requirements and connect it to a simple student profile.

  • Catalog-year student profile (completed courses, goals, interests)
  • Verified prerequisite and degree-rule snippets with sources
  • “Where do I stand?” progress view with missing-data flags
End of week

Deterministically explain completed vs. remaining requirements for one program, with sources and open questions.

WEEK 02 · AGENT

Ship the conversational counselor

Give advice with reasons—not just search results.

Build a tool-calling agent that clarifies goals, consults Week 1 tools and roster data, and compares options before recommending.

  • Clarify → consult → compare → explain conversation loop
  • Bounded tool calls with transparent action summaries
  • Source-backed “What should I take next, and why?” answers
End of week

A working counselor chat that produces a supported next-semester recommendation for a demo student profile.

WEEK 03 · PRODUCT

Counselor meets the planner

Turn a decision into an approvable semester.

Wire the existing schedule engine as an agent tool so advice becomes a reviewable calendar, alternatives, and student approval.

  • Conversation → validated section plan → calendar handoff
  • Reuse backup comparison and closure replanning as tools
  • Eval suite, uncertainty surfacing, and advisor-escalation stubs
Final product

End-to-end AI agent counselor: chat, recommend, schedule, and approve—for one program and one semester.

WEEK 3 FINAL PRODUCT

AI agent counselor — four questions, answered well.

Where do I stand?

Summarize completed courses and remaining requirements.

What should I take next?

Recommend courses using requirements, interests, and prerequisites.

Why this option?

Explain benefits, tradeoffs, and supporting official sources.

What if something changes?

Reassess the plan and propose alternatives for review.

Success looks like: a student can open a conversation, get a sourced recommendation, generate a conflict-free schedule, and approve a plan—without claiming graduation certification or enrollment authority. Scope stays one program, one semester.

How the agent works

Understand → Clarify → Consult sources & tools → Compare → Validate → Explain → Request approval → Remember

The interface centers on a counseling conversation beside an academic profile and recommendation panel. The calendar appears when the student is ready to lock in a semester.

Clear boundaries, useful handoffs.

  • Deterministic tools check schedule feasibility and explicitly modeled academic rules.
  • The AI explains and coordinates; it does not invent requirements or certify graduation eligibility.
  • Exceptions, transfer-credit decisions, and unclear policies go to a human advisor.
  • After week 3: durable accounts, multi-semester paths, and a broader student pilot—not required for the first counselor ship.
